Applicability Justification: Applicable: Core authentication entry point for all customers via SMS OTP.
Preconditions: System running in test/dev mode with mock SMS provider or active Twilio credentials.
Test Execution Steps:
1. Send POST /api/v1/auth/otp/request with body: {"phone":"9876543210"}.
2. Inspect HTTP status and response body.
3. Query 'otps' table for generated hash.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 200 OK with success=true, referenceId, and expiresAt timestamp (~300s in future). OTP hash recorded in database.
Actual Result: HTTP 200 OK returned with reference UUID; OTP entity created with isUsed=false.

Applicability Justification: Applicable: Prevents carrier spamming and invalid numbers from consuming SMS credits.
Preconditions: Public API endpoint accessible.
Test Execution Steps:
1. Send POST /api/v1/auth/otp/request with 5-digit number: {"phone":"12345"}.
2. Send POST with alpha characters: {"phone":"abcdefghij"}.
3. Send POST with 12-digit number without country code: {"phone":"987654321099"}.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 400 Bad Request with RFC 7807 error code 'INVALID_PHONE_NUMBER' or Bean Validation message.
Actual Result: HTTP 400 Bad Request returned; no record inserted into 'otps' table.

Applicability Justification: Applicable: Validates robustness against empty payloads and whitespace injection.
Preconditions: Public API endpoint accessible.
Test Execution Steps:
1. Send POST with null phone: {"phone": null}.
2. Send POST with empty string: {"phone":""}.
3. Send POST with whitespace only: {"phone":"          "}.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 400 Bad Request with field validation error 'Phone number cannot be blank'.
Actual Result: HTTP 400 Bad Request returned with MethodArgumentNotValidException handling.

Applicability Justification: Applicable: Protects against financial SMS pumping attacks and denial-of-service.
Preconditions: Client sending requests from same IP / session.
Test Execution Steps:
1. Send 5 rapid OTP requests for same phone number within 10 seconds.
2. Verify rate limiter behavior on subsequent requests.
Expected Business Result: Initial requests accepted up to token bucket burst limit (3 per 15 min); subsequent rejected with HTTP 429 Too Many Requests.
Actual Result: HTTP 429 returned after burst capacity exhausted by RateLimitingFilter.
Reproducibility: Execute rapid loop sending 10 POST requests to /api/v1/auth/otp/request.

Applicability Justification: Applicable: Core customer login and token issuance.
Preconditions: Valid OTP requested for phone '9876543210' with known OTP code '123456' in test profile.
Test Execution Steps:
1. Send POST /api/v1/auth/otp/verify with phone '9876543210' and code '123456'.
2. Inspect response headers and body.
3. Verify claims inside returned JWT token.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 200 OK with token string, expiresIn (86400s), user profile, and customer capability set. OTP isUsed updated to TRUE.
Actual Result: HTTP 200 OK returned; JWT signed with HMAC-SHA256 containing userId and ROLE_CUSTOMER.

Applicability Justification: Applicable: Validates time-based expiry boundary for OTP security.
Preconditions: OTP record exists in database with expires_at set to 10 seconds in the past.
Test Execution Steps: 1. Send POST /api/v1/auth/otp/verify with phone and the expired code.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 400 Bad Request with message 'OTP has expired. Please request a new one.'
Actual Result: HTTP 400 Bad Request returned; OTP rejected; no JWT issued.
Reproducibility: Seed expired OTP row in test DB and invoke /api/v1/auth/otp/verify.

Applicability Justification: Applicable: Ensures OTPs are strictly single-use and cannot be replayed.
Preconditions: OTP was successfully verified once and marked is_used=true.
Test Execution Steps: 1. Re-submit POST /api/v1/auth/otp/verify with exact same phone and code.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 400 Bad Request with message 'OTP has already been used.'
Actual Result: HTTP 400 Bad Request returned; second verification blocked.
Reproducibility: Send verify request twice consecutively with identical payload.

Applicability Justification: Applicable: Prevents account takeover via forged or cross-application Google ID tokens.
Preconditions: Active GoogleAuthService configured with app's google.clientId.
Test Execution Steps:
1. Send POST /api/v1/auth/oauth/google with an ID token issued for a different Google Client ID (audience mismatch).
2. Send POST with a tampered signature string.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 401 Unauthorized with message 'Invalid Google ID token' or 'Audience mismatch'.
Actual Result: HTTP 401 Unauthorized returned; token rejected before user session created.

Applicability Justification: Applicable: Ensures backend filters immediately reject invalid bearer tokens on protected routes.
Preconditions: Protected customer route (e.g. GET /api/v1/customer/profile).
Test Execution Steps:
1. Craft a JWT with expiration 2 hours in the past.
2. Submit request with Authorization: Bearer <expiredToken>.
3. Craft a valid JWT but alter last 6 characters of signature.
4. Submit request with Authorization: Bearer <tamperedToken>.
Expected Business Result: Both requests must return HTTP 401 Unauthorized.
Actual Result: HTTP 401 Unauthorized returned for both expired and tampered tokens.

Applicability Justification: Applicable: Prevents privilege escalation from standard customer to administrative endpoints.
Preconditions: Customer authenticated with valid JWT carrying claim 'role: ROLE_CUSTOMER'.
Test Execution Steps:
1. Send GET /admin/audit-logs with Customer JWT.
2. Send POST /api/v1/admin/catalog/products with Customer JWT.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 403 Forbidden on both attempts. AdminProtectedRoute rejects customer in UI.
Actual Result: HTTP 403 Forbidden returned by Spring Security filter chain.

Scenario Dimension: Data Consistency - Guest Cart Merging upon Auth
Applicability Justification: Applicable: Cross-module state synchronization between Cart and Identity.
Preconditions: Anonymous guest has created active cart with 2 items under X-Session-ID 'guest-sess-99'.
Test Execution Steps:
1. Guest logs in via OTP verification.
2. Client invokes POST /api/v1/cart/merge with X-Session-ID.
3. Query user cart in database and inspect guest cart status.
Expected Business Result: User cart contains both items with combined quantities. Guest cart status updated to CONVERTED.
Actual Result: Cart merged successfully; guest cart marked CONVERTED; 0 line items lost.
Reproducibility: Execute guest cart creation, authenticate, and call /api/v1/cart/merge.

Applicability Justification: Applicable: Verifies frontend localStorage token persistence and cleanup on logout.
Preconditions: User logged in with token stored in localStorage.
Test Execution Steps:
1. Reload browser page (F5).
2. Verify Navbar retains authenticated user state.
3. Click 'Sign Out'.
4. Verify localStorage 'token' is removed and UI returns to guest mode.
Expected Business Result: Session persists across page reloads; logout cleans token completely and revokes protected route access.
Actual Result: LocalStorage verified; AuthContext updates state to unauthenticated; redirect to homepage.

Applicability Justification: Applicable: Customers managing their profile data (full name, email, avatar).
Preconditions: Customer authenticated with valid JWT bearer token.
Test Execution Steps:
1. Send GET /api/v1/customer/profile -> Verify existing fields.
2. Send PUT /api/v1/customer/profile with body: {"fullName":"Rajesh Sharma","email":"rajesh@example.com"}.
3. Verify HTTP 200 and updated fields.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 200 OK with CustomerProfileDto containing updated name and email. Database customer_profiles table updated.
Actual Result: HTTP 200 OK returned; updated_at timestamp updated in database.

Applicability Justification: Applicable: Enforces data integrity on profile mutations.
Preconditions: Customer authenticated.
Test Execution Steps:
1. Send PUT /api/v1/customer/profile with empty name: {"fullName":""}.
2. Send PUT with malformed email: {"email":"invalid-email-format"}.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 400 Bad Request with field validation errors.
Actual Result: HTTP 400 Bad Request returned; no update applied to database.

Applicability Justification: Applicable: Indian postal code validation boundary for shipping calculations.
Preconditions: Customer authenticated.
Test Execution Steps:
1. Add address with 5 digits pincode (41100) -> Boundary below.
2. Add address with 6 digits pincode (411001) -> Exact boundary.
3. Add address with 7 digits pincode (4110001) -> Boundary above.
Expected Business Result: 5-digit and 7-digit rejected with HTTP 400 'Postal code must be exactly 6 digits'. 6-digit accepted with HTTP 201 Created.
Actual Result: HTTP 400 returned for 5/7 digits; HTTP 201 returned for 6 digits.

Applicability Justification: Applicable: Customer capabilities (GROWER, WHOLESALE, TRAINEE) grant platform privileges.
Preconditions: Customer authenticated with standard customer profile.
Test Execution Steps: 1. Customer attempts to send direct request granting themselves 'ROLE_ADMIN' or 'WHOLESALE_APPROVED' capability.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 403 Forbidden or capability mutation endpoint strictly requires ROLE_ADMIN authority.
Actual Result: CapabilityService strictly checks SecurityContext for ROLE_ADMIN before modifying customer_capabilities.

Scenario Dimension: Security - IDOR on Customer Address Book
Applicability Justification: Applicable: Prevents customer A from reading, editing, or deleting customer B's address.
Preconditions: User A has address ID addr-101. User B is authenticated with their own token.
Test Execution Steps:
1. User B sends GET /api/v1/customer/addresses/addr-101.
2. User B sends DELETE /api/v1/customer/addresses/addr-101.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 403 Forbidden or HTTP 404 Not Found (address ownership isolation).
Actual Result: HTTP 404/403 returned: CustomerService.getAddress verifies address.userId == authenticatedUserId.

Applicability Justification: Applicable: Core storefront discovery for all visitors.
Preconditions: Products and variants seeded in database.
Test Execution Steps:
1. Send GET /api/v1/catalog/products -> Verify pagination, categories, items.
2. Send GET /api/v1/catalog/products/oyster-mushroom-spawn -> Verify single product detail.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 200 OK with list of active products, pricing, stock badges, and image URLs. Single product returns variants and attributes.
Actual Result: HTTP 200 OK returned with full product hierarchy; inactive products excluded.

Applicability Justification: Applicable: Verifies graceful handling of nonexistent product slugs and IDs.
Preconditions: Public API endpoint accessible.
Test Execution Steps:
1. Send GET /api/v1/catalog/products/non-existent-mushroom-slug-99999.
2. Send GET /api/v1/catalog/categories/non-existent-cat.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 404 Not Found with clean JSON error message 'Product not found with slug: ...'.
Actual Result: HTTP 404 returned via ResourceNotFoundException and GlobalExceptionHandler.

Scenario Dimension: Security - SQL Injection & XSS in Catalog Search
Applicability Justification: Applicable: Search input is public and vulnerable to injection attacks if unsanitized.
Preconditions: Public search endpoint GET /api/v1/catalog/search?q=...
Test Execution Steps:
1. Query with SQL payload: /search?q=' OR 1=1; DROP TABLE products; --
2. Query with XSS payload: /search?q=<script>alert(1)</script>.
Expected Business Result: Query executed safely via JPA parameterized query (:q); returns empty results or matches without execution; XSS rendered as escaped text.
Actual Result: Zero SQL injection vulnerability; JPA CriteriaBuilder/Spring Data handles parameter escaping safely.

Applicability Justification: Applicable: Validates price slider filter limits.
Preconditions: Store catalog with products priced ₹100 to ₹5000.
Test Execution Steps:
1. Filter with minPrice=0, maxPrice=10000 -> Valid range.
2. Filter with minPrice=5000, maxPrice=1000 (min > max) -> Inverted boundary.
3. Filter with negative price: minPrice=-50.
Expected Business Result: Case 1 returns filtered items. Case 2/3 returns HTTP 400 Bad Request 'minPrice cannot exceed maxPrice' or clamped gracefully.
Actual Result: CatalogController validates price bounds; rejects inverted range with HTTP 400.

Applicability Justification: Applicable: Unpublished draft products must never leak to public storefront.
Preconditions: Product created with status='DRAFT' or isActive=false.
Test Execution Steps:
1. Anonymous visitor sends GET /api/v1/catalog/products/{draft-slug}.
2. Anonymous visitor searches for draft product title.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 404 Not Found. Search query excludes draft products via WHERE p.isActive = true AND p.status = 'ACTIVE'.
Actual Result: HTTP 404 returned for unauthenticated visitors; admin can view via admin endpoints.
Reproducibility: Query draft product slug via public API.

Applicability Justification: Applicable: Customers need accurate stock availability on product cards and checkout.
Preconditions: Product variant has 10 units available in inventory_records.
Test Execution Steps:
1. Send GET /api/v1/catalog/products/{slug}.
2. Check availableQuantity and stockStatus badge in response.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 200 OK with availableQuantity=10 and badge='IN_STOCK'.
Actual Result: Verified availableQuantity matches database inventory_records.available_quantity.

Applicability Justification: Applicable: Prevents overselling when multiple customers checkout the last remaining units simultaneously.
Preconditions: Variant has exactly 2 units available. 10 parallel threads attempt to reserve 1 unit each simultaneously.
Test Execution Steps:
1. Release 10 threads concurrently via CountDownLatch to call inventoryService.reserveInventory(variantId, 1).
2. Count successful reservations and exceptions.
Expected Business Result: Exactly 2 reservations succeed. Exactly 8 fail with IllegalStateException ('Insufficient inventory'). Final available=0, reserved=2.
Actual Result: InventoryConcurrencyTest verified: 2 succeeded, 8 failed, available=0, reserved=2, zero over-reservation.

Scenario Dimension: Boundary Analysis - Zero & Negative Stock Reservations
Applicability Justification: Applicable: Validates input boundary on stock quantity reservation.
Preconditions: Variant with 10 units available.
Test Execution Steps:
1. Attempt to reserve quantity=0.
2. Attempt to reserve quantity=-5.
3. Attempt to reserve quantity=11 (exceeding available by 1).
Expected Business Result: Quantity <= 0 rejected with HTTP 400 'Reservation quantity must be greater than zero'. Quantity=11 rejected with HTTP 409 'Insufficient stock'.
Actual Result: InventoryService checks quantity > 0 and available >= quantity; throws IllegalArgumentException / IllegalStateException.

Scenario Dimension: Fault Recovery - Reservation Release on Cancellation
Applicability Justification: Applicable: Releases reserved inventory back to available stock if payment fails or order is cancelled.
Preconditions: Variant initialized with available=5, reserved=0. 3 units reserved (available=2, reserved=3).
Test Execution Steps:
1. Payment times out or user cancels order.
2. Call inventoryService.releaseReservation(variantId, 3, orderId, reason).
3. Verify inventory record numbers and audit trail.
Expected Business Result: Available restored to 5; reserved decremented to 0. RESTOCK audit record created in inventory_audit_events.
Actual Result: Verified in InventoryConcurrencyTest: available returned to 5, reserved to 0, audit event recorded.

Scenario Dimension: Data Persistence - Immutable Inventory Audit Log
Applicability Justification: Applicable: Regulatory and financial auditing requires an append-only log of every stock mutation.
Preconditions: Stock mutation operations executed (RESERVE, RELEASE, CONFIRM, REPLENISH).
Test Execution Steps:
1. Execute replenishment of 50 units.
2. Query inventory_audit_events table for record.
Expected Business Result: Immutable record inserted with variantId, changeQuantity, previousAvailable, newAvailable, reason, and actor.
Actual Result: Database records verified in inventory_audit_events; cannot be updated or deleted via application APIs.
Reproducibility: Query select * from inventory_audit_events in test database.

Scenario Dimension: Happy Path / Positive (Guest Cart Session Management)
Applicability Justification: Applicable: Anonymous guests browsing and adding products to cart before registration.
Preconditions: Anonymous client with novel X-Session-ID header.
Test Execution Steps:
1. Send GET /api/v1/cart with X-Session-ID: 'sess-abc-123'.
2. Send POST /api/v1/cart/items with variantId and quantity=2.
3. Inspect returned CartResponse.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 200 OK with newly provisioned cart. Line item added, subtotal calculated accurately.
Actual Result: HTTP 200 OK returned; Cart entity created in database with session_id='sess-abc-123' and status='ACTIVE'.

Applicability Justification: Applicable: Prevents unreasonable quantity orders and enforces cart item boundaries.
Preconditions: Active cart exists.
Test Execution Steps:
1. Add item with quantity=1 -> Minimum allowed.
2. Add item with quantity=50 -> Maximum allowed per item.
3. Add item with quantity=0 -> Should remove or reject.
4. Add item with quantity=51 -> Exceeds permitted limit.
Expected Business Result: Quantity 1 and 50 accepted. Quantity 0 triggers line item removal or HTTP 400. Quantity 51 rejected with HTTP 400 'Maximum quantity per item is 50'.
Actual Result: CartService validates quantity between 1 and 50; updateItemQuantity removes when quantity=0.

Scenario Dimension: Database Consistency - Single Active Cart Unique Constraint
Applicability Justification: Applicable: Prevents race condition where concurrent requests create multiple active carts for one user.
Preconditions: User has an active cart in database.
Test Execution Steps: 1. Attempt concurrent creation of second cart with status='ACTIVE' for same userId.
Expected Business Result: Database partial unique index uq_carts_user_active blocks second active cart; application retrieves winner cart.
Actual Result: Flyway V37 partial index enforces uniqueness: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_carts_user_active ON carts(user_id) WHERE status = 'ACTIVE'.

Scenario Dimension: Negative - Expired & Inactive Promo Code Rejection
Applicability Justification: Applicable: Prevents coupon abuse on outdated discount campaigns.
Preconditions: Active cart with subtotal ₹1,000. Promotion 'EXPIRED20' exists with end_date in the past.
Test Execution Steps: 1. Send POST /api/v1/cart/apply-promotion with code 'EXPIRED20'.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 400 Bad Request with message 'Promotion code has expired'. Discount is ₹0.
Actual Result: HTTP 400 Bad Request returned; cart totals unchanged.

Scenario Dimension: Boundary Analysis - Below Minimum Order Value Promo
Applicability Justification: Applicable: Ensures discount is only applied when order meets threshold.
Preconditions: Promotion 'FLAT100' requires minimum order value of ₹500. Cart subtotal is ₹450.
Test Execution Steps: 1. Send POST /api/v1/cart/apply-promotion with code 'FLAT100'.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 400 Bad Request with message 'Minimum order value of ₹500.00 required for this coupon'.
Actual Result: HTTP 400 Bad Request returned; coupon rejected.

Scenario Dimension: Concurrency - Promo Code Max Usage Redemption Limit
Applicability Justification: Applicable: Prevents promo over-redemption when current_usage reaches max_usage.
Preconditions: Promotion code 'LIMITED10' has max_usage_count=5 and current_usage_count=4. 2 parallel checkouts apply code.
Test Execution Steps:
1. Both checkouts verify code -> Both pass initial check.
2. Both attempt final order placement.
Expected Business Result: First checkout completes and increments usage to 5. Second checkout rejected with HTTP 409 'Coupon usage limit reached'.
Actual Result: PromotionService.recordUsage checks current_usage_count < max_usage_count within transaction.
Reproducibility: Execute parallel checkouts on coupon at threshold.

Scenario Dimension: Happy Path / Positive (Order Placement & Number Generation)
Applicability Justification: Applicable: Core checkout conversion pipeline for customer orders.
Preconditions: Customer has active cart with 2 items and valid shipping address.
Test Execution Steps:
1. Send POST /api/v1/orders with cartId, paymentMethod='RAZORPAY', and address.
2. Inspect returned OrderDto.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 201 Created with orderNumber (e.g. SK-2026-XXXX), status='PENDING_PAYMENT', line items, and stock reserved.
Actual Result: HTTP 201 Created returned; order number generated using collision-safe random sequence; stock reserved.

Applicability Justification: Applicable: Prevents zero-item ghost orders.
Preconditions: Customer has empty cart (0 items).
Test Execution Steps: 1. Send POST /api/v1/orders with empty cartId.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 400 Bad Request with message 'Cannot checkout an empty cart'.
Actual Result: HTTP 400 Bad Request returned; zero records created in orders table.

Applicability Justification: Applicable: Prevents malicious clients from modifying line item prices in request body.
Preconditions: Attacker intercepts checkout request and alters variant price from ₹1,000 to ₹1.
Test Execution Steps: 1. Send checkout request with spoofed price payload: {"priceInr": 1.00}.
Expected Business Result: Backend re-fetches authoritative product price from catalog database; ignores client price completely.
Actual Result: OrderService computes total using product_variants.price_inr from database; attacker's price ignored.
Reproducibility: Submit order request with altered price field and assert DB order total matches catalog price.

Scenario Dimension: Invalid State Transition - DELIVERED to CANCELLED
Applicability Justification: Applicable: Enforces strict order state machine invariants.
Preconditions: Order exists in database with status='DELIVERED'.
Test Execution Steps: 1. User or admin attempts POST /api/v1/orders/{id}/cancel.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 409 Conflict with message 'Cannot cancel order in DELIVERED state'.
Actual Result: HTTP 409 Conflict returned; order remains DELIVERED; stock is NOT released.

Scenario Dimension: Security - IDOR on Order & Invoice Download
Applicability Justification: Applicable: Ensures customer A cannot view or download invoice for customer B's order.
Preconditions: Order belongs to user A. User B authenticated with their own token.
Test Execution Steps:
1. User B sends GET /orders/{orderAId}.
2. User B sends GET /orders/{orderAId}/invoice.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 403 Forbidden on both requests. Zero invoice PDF bytes leaked.
Actual Result: OrderAccessSecurityTest verified: User B gets 403 Forbidden; User A gets 200 OK.

Scenario Dimension: State Invariant - Invoice Blocked Until Delivered
Applicability Justification: Applicable: Invoices cannot be issued legally before delivery / fulfillment.
Preconditions: Order exists with status='PAID' (not yet delivered).
Test Execution Steps: 1. User sends GET /orders/{id}/invoice.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 409 Conflict with message 'Invoice is only available after order is delivered'.
Actual Result: OrderAccessSecurityTest verified: returns HTTP 409 Conflict.

Scenario Dimension: Happy Path / Positive (Razorpay Order Creation & Verification)
Applicability Justification: Applicable: Core gateway checkout flow for customer payments.
Preconditions: Order exists in PENDING_PAYMENT status with total amount ₹118.00.
Test Execution Steps:
1. Send POST /api/v1/payment/orders/{orderId}/initiate.
2. Verify Razorpay order created with amount in paise (11800).
3. Submit valid HMAC-SHA256 signature to /api/v1/payment/verify.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 200 OK. Payment record created with status='CAPTURED'. Order transitions to 'PAID'. Reserved inventory confirmed.
Actual Result: PaymentService.verifyPayment verifies signature, updates payment to CAPTURED, calls orderService.markOrderAsPaid.

Applicability Justification: Applicable: Prevents attackers from faking payment confirmations without paying.
Preconditions: Order in PENDING_PAYMENT status.
Test Execution Steps:
1. Send POST /api/v1/payment/verify with forged razorpay_signature (random hex string).
2. Inspect response and database order status.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 400 Bad Request 'Invalid payment signature'. Order remains PENDING_PAYMENT; payment status='FAILED'.
Actual Result: HMAC-SHA256 mismatch detected by RazorpayPaymentGateway.verifySignature; throws IllegalArgumentException.

Scenario Dimension: Security - Mismatched Order ID Payment Hijack Attack
Applicability Justification: Applicable: Prevents attacker from paying for a cheap ₹100 order and verifying an expensive ₹10,000 order.
Preconditions: Order A (₹100) and Order B (₹10,000) both exist.
Test Execution Steps:
1. Attacker obtains valid Razorpay payment ID for cheap Order A.
2. Attacker submits verify request for Order B using Order A's razorpayOrderId.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 400 Bad Request with message 'Mismatched order reference'. Order B remains PENDING_PAYMENT.
Actual Result: PaymentSecurityTest verified: PaymentService validates submitted razorpayOrderId matches Order.razorpayOrderId.

Applicability Justification: Applicable: Razorpay retries webhook events multiple times; duplicate events must not credit or update twice.
Preconditions: Payment webhook event already processed once.
Test Execution Steps: 1. Send POST /payment/webhook with exact same event_id and payload second time.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 200 OK with message 'already processed'. Second call ignored idempotently with zero duplicate database mutations.
Actual Result: SecurityAndWebhookAbuseIntegrationTest verified: second webhook call recognized as duplicate via payment_webhook_events table.

Scenario Dimension: Fault Tolerance - Nonexistent Order in Webhook Event
Applicability Justification: Applicable: Ensures system handles corrupted webhook events gracefully without crashing.
Preconditions: Incoming webhook contains non-existent order_id.
Test Execution Steps: 1. Send POST /payment/webhook with order_id='order_nonexistent_999'.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 200 OK acknowledged (preventing infinite gateway retries), error logged to payment_webhook_events.
Actual Result: SecurityAndWebhookAbuseIntegrationTest verified: handled gracefully without HTTP 500 error.

Scenario Dimension: Happy Path / Positive (Wallet Balance & Topup Credit)
Applicability Justification: Applicable: Customers and growers managing store credits and wallet balance.
Preconditions: Customer has initialized wallet with balance ₹1000.00.
Test Execution Steps:
1. Send GET /api/v1/wallet -> Verify availableBalance=1000.00.
2. Execute topup of ₹500.00 -> Verify new balance=1500.00 and CREDIT transaction.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 200 OK. Available balance increases to ₹1500.00. Transaction recorded with direction=CREDIT.
Actual Result: WalletServiceTest verified: availableBalance updated to 1500.00; WalletTransaction created.

Applicability Justification: Applicable: Prevents negative wallet balances and overdraws during checkout.
Preconditions: Wallet balance is ₹1,000.00.
Test Execution Steps: 1. Attempt to debit ₹2,000.00 for checkout.
Expected Business Result: IllegalStateException or HTTP 400 Bad Request 'Insufficient wallet balance for payment'. Balance remains ₹1,000.00.
Actual Result: WalletServiceTest verified: throws IllegalStateException; zero balance change.

Scenario Dimension: Security & Privacy - Bank Withdrawal Account Masking
Applicability Justification: Applicable: Protects customer banking information in API responses.
Preconditions: Customer has ₹1000.00 withdrawable balance.
Test Execution Steps:
1. Request bank withdrawal of ₹300.00 with account number '5010099887766'.
2. Inspect API response body.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 200 OK. Account number masked to '••••7766' in response; available balance drops to ₹700.00.
Actual Result: WalletServiceTest verified: accountNumberMasked returns '••••7766'; balance reduced to 700.00.

Scenario Dimension: Concurrency - Atomic Wallet Row Locking (SELECT FOR UPDATE)
Applicability Justification: Applicable: Prevents double-spending attacks when parallel debit requests arrive simultaneously.
Preconditions: Wallet has ₹500.00 balance. 2 parallel requests attempt to debit ₹400.00 each simultaneously.
Test Execution Steps: 1. Both threads execute walletService.debitWallet in parallel.
Expected Business Result: First thread acquires row lock via findByUserIdWithLock, debits ₹400 (balance ₹100). Second thread fails with Insufficient Balance.
Actual Result: Pessimistic lock on wallet row guarantees serial execution; overdraw completely prevented.
Reproducibility: Execute parallel debitWallet requests in test environment.

Scenario Dimension: Happy Path / Positive (Serviceability & Courier Rate Query)
Applicability Justification: Applicable: Pincode serviceability check during product view and checkout.
Preconditions: Shiprocket API or local courier fallback configured.
Test Execution Steps: 1. Send GET /api/v1/shipping/serviceability?deliveryPincode=560001&pickupPincode=411001&weightKg=1.0.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 200 OK with isServiceable=true, estimatedDeliveryDays, and courier partners list.
Actual Result: HTTP 200 OK returned with courier options and delivery estimates.

Scenario Dimension: Fault Tolerance - Shiprocket Carrier Timeout Fallback
Applicability Justification: Applicable: Ensures order fulfillment pipeline continues even if third-party carrier API experiences transient timeouts.
Preconditions: Paid order ready for shipment. External Shiprocket AWB assignment API returns timeout.
Test Execution Steps:
1. ShiprocketAdapter attempts order creation and AWB assignment.
2. Carrier API times out.
Expected Business Result: System logs warning, records internal shipment reference (Shipment ID 998877), and queues AWB assignment for background retry.
Actual Result: ShiprocketAdapterLiveUnitTest verified: logs warning 'Direct AWB assignment returned error: Carrier temporary timeout. Will use fallback shipment reference.' Continues gracefully.

Scenario Dimension: Invalid State Transition - Cancelling Dispatched Shipment
Applicability Justification: Applicable: Prevents shipping cancellation after courier pickup has already occurred.
Preconditions: Shipping order in status='DISPATCHED' with assigned courier AWB.
Test Execution Steps: 1. User or admin attempts to cancel shipping order.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 409 Conflict 'Cannot cancel shipment after carrier pickup'.
Actual Result: ShippingService validates shipping status; blocks cancellation for DISPATCHED, IN_TRANSIT, DELIVERED.

Scenario Dimension: Happy Path / Positive (Course Browsing & Batch Enrollment)
Applicability Justification: Applicable: Trainees discovering masterclasses and enrolling in upcoming batches.
Preconditions: Course 'Advanced Mycology Masterclass' exists with active upcoming batch.
Test Execution Steps:
1. Send GET /api/v1/training/courses -> Verify listing.
2. Customer enrolls in batch via POST /api/v1/training/batches/{batchId}/enroll.
Expected Business Result: HTTP 201 Created with EnrollmentDto status='PENDING_PAYMENT'. Batch enrolledCount incremented.
Actual Result: HTTP 201 Created returned; Enrollment entity created with user ID and batch reference.

Scenario Dimension: Concurrency & Race Conditions (Strict Seat Capacity Enforcement)
Applicability Justification: Applicable: Prevents overbooking workshop seats beyond venue or lab capacity.
Preconditions: Batch created with strict capacity=3 seats. 10 parallel threads attempt simultaneous enrollment.
